long_biography.plain_text:
Outdoor advertising executive Drew Katz saw specially designed venues as a way for smaller companies to compete with national rivals. With business partner John Foster, he developed a project around Oakland's arena and coliseum that shared advertising revenue with the city and county. Negotiations and planning took more than two years before construction began.

Architect Ian Birchall designed the advertising structures to complement the sports buildings. They included tall billboard towers, kiosks and gateways with rotating signs. Katz argued that distinctive, well-designed installations could address municipal concerns about new advertising. Nissan used three consecutive billboards at the site to reveal different views of a new car.
